title: Technique rules (techniques/<id>/technique.yaml)
description: Machine-readable rules for one testing technique: what calls for it (needed_when), what makes it possible (possible_when), what rules it out or postpones it (reject_or_defer_when), checks to run first, and what to use instead. The technique decision tool reads these to mark each technique for a repo. Lessons are not recorded here: each lesson, in the lessons repo (under-test-lessons), names the technique ids it teaches in its own lesson.yaml, and that repo's build checks the two agree. Renaming or removing a technique id therefore needs the same change in the lessons repo. Words follow GLOSSARY.md.

maturityLevel.description: A test maturity level (see the decision guide: what each test maturity level means): 0 builds reliably; 1 runs on its own; 2 current behaviour recorded; 3 checked against requirements; 4 tests proven to catch bugs; 5 checked in production.

id.description: Folder name; used in tt:technique/<id> labels and in decisions: entries.

needed_when.description: Conditions that say the technique is wanted. Any one known true calls for it. If every one is known false, the technique is rejected; if none is known true but one is unknown, it is deferred. Each is quoted word for word in reasons, so keep its wording stable.

possible_when.description: Conditions that say the technique can be done. To adopt, every one must hold or be planned work. One that is unknown, or false and not planned work, defers the technique. Each is quoted word for word in reasons, so keep its wording stable.

reject_or_defer_when.description: Facts that rule the technique out or postpone it. One known true rejects it when it is about the framework, a vendor, a licence or who owns what, and defers it otherwise; one that is unknown defers it. A condition the repo's files don't mention counts as false. A fact goes in only one of needed_when, possible_when and reject_or_defer_when: a fact that is true now but planned work will change goes here, and what makes the technique possible goes in possible_when.

done_by.description: tool: an automated check. person: needs someone's sign-off.

outside_approval.description: true when the check is an approval or agreement from outside the team doing the work: a provider team, a licence, the scope, security, or capture in an environment. While it isn't given, the technique is deferred. Every other check is part of the work and never defers it.

fallback.description: What to use instead if rejected. A technique id where one exists, otherwise plain words.

workstream.description: The workstream whose issues this technique's work goes into. Roughly in this order: make it run on its own, fix flaky tests, record current behaviour, make code testable, test against requirements, strengthen tests, check in production.

test_stand_in_approach.description: Only for techniques in the make-it-run-on-its-own workstream: which test stand-in approach this technique implements.

evidence_for_maturity_levels.description: Which test maturity levels a repo can claim on the strength of tests produced by this technique. Example: Testcontainers tests can count towards levels 1 to 3; mutation testing is the evidence for level 4.

application_types.description: Application types whose testing guides adopt this by default. For information only; the testing guides are authoritative.

references.description: Anchors in docs/REFERENCES.md that give the background for this technique.
